question.problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2},\, & -1\le x\le 1,\,\,-1\le y\le 2, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

If $\text{E}[X]=0$ and $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{5}{4},$ find the covariance matrix for $X$ and $Y.$
question.worked_solution:
For two random variables $X$ and $Y,$ the covariance matrix $Σ$ is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}].
$$

Recall that the variance of a random variable $X$ is determined by the formula

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}.
$$

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2})\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{y}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{4}\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{y}^{2}\cdot {[\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}]}_{-1}^{1}\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}]}_{-1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}-{(0)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, we compute $\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]$ using the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{Y}^{2}] & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}\cdot f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}(\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2})\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{y}^{4}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{y}^{4}{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{-1}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-1}^{2}{y}^{4}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot {[\frac{1}{5}{y}^{5}]}_{-1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{33}{5} \\  & =\frac{11}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}]-\text{E}[Y]^{2} \\  & =\frac{11}{5}-{(\frac{5}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{51}{80}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$ The joint support of $X$ and $Y$ is given by the rectangle

$$
S=[-1,1]\times [-1,2].
$$

Moreover, we can write

$$
f(x,y)=g(x)\cdot h(y),
$$

where $g(x)=\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}$ and $h(y)=\frac{{y}^{2}}{3}.$

Hence, $X$ and $Y$ are independent, and consequently $\text{Cov}[X,Y]=0.$

Therefore, the covariance matrix is given by

$$
Σ=[\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & \text{Cov}[X,Y] \\ \text{Cov}[Y,X] & \text{Var}[Y]\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{5} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{51}{80}\end{aligned}].
$$
